subject: Re: Pinecrest MAP & procurement checklist — AWS vs GCP billing path
messages:
From: Liz Carter <liz.carter@pinecresthealth.org>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@pinecresthealth.org
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pinecrest MAP request — private offer/billing questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and how Redwood handles quantized models. Procurement asked me to send a simple mutual action plan (MAP) so we can align approvals and the billing route.

Key asks from our side:
- Can you outline the recommended path for an AWS Private Offer vs GCP Marketplace private pricing? We need to understand timing differences for PO approval and invoicing cadence.
- Is billing via marketplace (PO -> AWS invoice) supported while we keep data in our VPC (private deployment)? Any constraints?
- A rough timeline for evaluation milestones (tech validation, security signoff, legal review, PO) — our target is go-live by mid-November.

If you can send a one-page MAP and any template SOW or billing notes, that would help speed internal approvals.

Attaching our procurement intake template (procurement@pinecresthealth.org) to make it easier.

Best,
Liz Carter
Director of AI Platforms
Pinecrest Health

Attachment: pinecrest_procurement_intake.xlsx (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Liz Carter <liz.carter@pinecresthealth.org>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pinecrest MAP request — private offer/billing questions

Hi Liz — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the intake template. I put together an initial MAP and a short note on the two billing paths (attached). High level:

- Recommendation: For fastest procurement and consistent PO-to-invoice flow, AWS Private Offer will usually get you to invoicing faster if you already have an AWS billing relationship. GCP private offers are comparable but often require a separate Cloud Billing Account setup which can add 1–2 weeks.
- Data locality: Both AWS and GCP marketplace private offers support Redwood Private where the control plane is in your VPC and data never leaves your environment. We map the license/billing to the marketplace contract; no runtime data is exchanged for billing purposes.
- Timeline (tentative):
  1) Technical eval (SRE + Sec): 1 week (we provide quick-start env + perf runbook)
  2) Security questionnaire & evidence: 1–2 weeks (we have SOC2, audit logs export sample)
  3) Legal/Commercial review & SOW redline: 1 week
  4) PO issuance & marketplace onboarding: 1–2 weeks (depends on vendor)

I attached: Pinecrest-MAP-v1.xlsx (MAP with milestone owners) and a draft SOW.

Next steps:
- Can you confirm procurement contact and whether Pinecrest prefers AWS billing or GCP?
- Aditya / Karthik — looping you to confirm any special billing configurations (commit vs usage invoicing) we should include.

I can also schedule a MAP kickoff call tomorrow afternoon if that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Pinecrest-MAP-v1.xlsx, SOW-draft-pinecrest.pdf

Folks — quick read: the MAP looks good. Couple of operational notes to include before we send to procurement:

- For AWS Private Offers we can enable marketplace invoicing that bills Pinecrest directly on AWS invoices; if Pinecrest wants a Redwood invoice instead we need to route through our finance and set up a reseller arrangement (adds ~2 weeks). We should capture their preference.
- If they are evaluating both AWS & GCP in parallel, call out the recommended fallback policy: start with AWS Private Offer (if they have an AWS billing account), and fallback to a Direct Redwood invoice or GCP private offer if AWS gating becomes a blocker.
- Add an explicit acceptance gate for performance (99th pct latency target) and an integration checkpoint for KV cache warmup so their SRE can validate throughput under realistic load.

Action items I suggest adding to the MAP spreadsheet:
- OWNER: Redwood AE (Marissa) — coordinate procurement
- OWNER: Redwood SE (Karthik) — technical sign-off + perf runbook
- OWNER: Pinecrest SRE (Liz) — tech validation and KV warmup test
- OWNER: Procurement (procurement@pinecresthealth.org) — PO issuance

I can prepare a short clause about reseller vs marketplace billing to attach to the SOW draft.

-Aditya
Sr. Product Manager, Platform Economics
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pinecrest MAP request — technical validation notes

Liz / team — quick technical note to speed the eval:

- We'll provision a short-lived Redwood Private sandbox in your AWS account (IAM role + VPC peering guide) for the perf run. This avoids egress and lets you validate KV cache behavior.
- Test matrix I propose (we'll provide a script): 3 workload patterns (chat, long context generation, embeddings) with 500 concurrent users ramped over 10 minutes. Targets: median latency < 180ms, p99 < 800ms for the chat profile.
- Evidence package we can supply in 24–48 hours: SOC2 excerpt, audit-logs sample, packet listing for the VPC peering setup, and the perf runbook.

I'll attach the perf script and an example infra checklist to the Drive link. Once procurement confirms billing path we can lock in dates.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — procurement here. We prefer the AWS Private Offer route since Pinecrest already routes cloud costs through AWS. Our finance team prefers invoicing on the AWS invoice (marketplace flow) rather than a separate Redwood invoice.

Please include the marketplace-invoice option in the MAP and confirm:
- Will marketplace invoicing cover any committed discount? (if we commit to 12 months)
- Do we need a reseller agreement to have usage-level discounts reflected?

Procurement contact: Anita Ramos <anita.ramos@pinecresthealth.org> (CC'd on separate thread).

Thanks,
